# oxide_parse

[![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/oxide-parse)](https://pypi.org/project/oxide-parse/)
[![CI](https://github.com/M-16gt/oxide_parse/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/M-16gt/oxide_parse/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![MIT license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE)

Declarative HTML and JSON extraction engine in Rust with a Python API: you describe a schema with `T`, compile it to a JSON-serializable IR, and run it in a single streaming pass or over a DOM.

Three things that set it apart:
- **Streaming engine (`stream`) without a DOM:** common schemas (catalogs, metadata, embedded JSON) run in a single pass over bytes, keeping only the open tag stack and extracted values in memory.
- **Schema as serializable IR:** save any plan to JSON or YAML (`to_json()`) and turn it back into plain Python (`to_python()`).
- **Zero-IO `Session`:** the core never performs network requests or LLM calls — it yields URLs (`follow`, `paginate`) and broken selectors (`adaptive` + `repair_batch`) to your sync or async code.

## Installation

```bash
pip install oxide-parse
```

From source (Rust 1.74+ and Python 3.9+):

```bash
uv sync && uv run maturin develop --release --features full
```

## Quick Example

```python
from oxide_parse import T, compile

html = """
<html><body>
  <h1>Laptops</h1>
  <script id="__NEXT_DATA__" type="application/json">{"currency": "USD"}</script>
  <div class="card"><h2>ThinkPad X1</h2><span class="price">$1,299.50</span></div>
  <div class="card"><h2>Broken</h2><span class="price">out of stock</span></div>
</body></html>
"""

schema = {
    "title": T.css("h1").text(),
    "currency": T.css("script#__NEXT_DATA__").text().parse_json()["currency"],
    "items": T.css(".card").map({
        "name": T.css("h2").text(),
        "price": T.css(".price").text().float(),
    }, on_error="skip"),
}

plan = compile(schema, backend="auto")
data = plan.extract_detailed(html)
print(plan.engine, data.data, data.errors, sep="\n")
```

```text
stream
{'title': 'Laptops', 'currency': 'USD', 'items': [{'name': 'ThinkPad X1', 'price': 1299.5}]}
[{'path': '$.items[1].price', 'message': 'float: no number in "out of stock"'}]
```

## Choosing an Engine

| `backend=` | Kind | When to use | DOM | XPath | `:scope` | `adaptive` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `auto` | automatic | almost always (`stream`, falls back to DOM when needed) | as needed | yes | yes | yes |
| `stream` | streaming | catalogs, `<head>` metadata, large pages | no | no | yes | no |
| `lite` | arena DOM | complex CSS, `:contains()`, XPath, `distill()` | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| `scraper` | html5ever DOM | malformed HTML needing exact HTML5 tree rules | yes | yes | no | yes |
| `json` | data | same schemas over JSON documents | no | no | no | no |
| `xml` | XML DOM | XML documents and XPath selectors | yes | yes | no | no |

## Highlights

**Hybrid HTML + JSON** (`__NEXT_DATA__`, JS state, JSON-LD, OpenGraph):

```python
hy_html = '<head><meta property="og:title" content="X1"></head><script id="s">window.__S__={"n":3}</script>'
hy_schema = {"og": T.meta_tags(values="first")["og:title"], "n": T.css("script#s").text().js_json("window.__S__")["n"]}
print(compile(hy_schema, backend="auto").extract(hy_html))
```

```text
{'og': 'X1', 'n': 3}
```

**Self-healing selectors & Python code patching** (`adaptive` + `extract_or_repair` + `to_python()`):

```python
p_adapt = compile({"price": T.css(".price", adaptive="price").text().float()})
p_adapt.extract('<div id="p1"><span class="price">$100</span></div>')
res = p_adapt.extract_or_repair('<section><div><strong class="cost">$95</strong></div></section>', repair=lambda _: {"price": ".cost"})
print(res.data, res.plan.to_python().splitlines()[-2].strip())
```

```text
{'price': 95.0} 'price': T.css('.cost', adaptive='price').text().float(),
```

**Zero-IO `follow` / `paginate` and Rayon `extract_batch` (GIL released):**

```python
from oxide_parse import follow, paginate

pages = {"https://ex.test/1": "<b>42</b><a class='next' href='/2'>n</a>", "https://ex.test/2": "<b>9</b>"}
f_plan = compile({"vals": follow(T.css("a").attr("href").url(), paginate(T.css("b").map(T.text().int()), T.css("a.next").attr("href").url()))})
print(f_plan.extract('<a href="/1">x</a>', meta={"base_url": "https://ex.test"}, fetch=lambda url, **_: pages[url]))
print(compile({"n": T.css("b").text().int()}, backend="auto").extract_batch(["<b>1</b>", "<b>x</b>"], errors="collect"))
```

```text
{'vals': [42, 9]}
([{'n': 1}, None], [{'index': 1, 'message': 'extraction error at `$.n`: int: no number in "x"'}])
```

**LLM preparation (`distill`, `markdown`) and deterministic migration without an LLM:**

```python
from oxide_parse import distill, markdown, migrate

print(markdown("<article><h1>Title</h1><p class='ad'>Ad</p><p>Text</p></article>", "article", without=".ad"))
print(migrate.from_selector_map_code({"title": "h1::text", "tags": ["li::text"]}).splitlines()[-3].strip())
```

```text
# Title

Text
'title': T.css('h1').text().strip(),
```

## Benchmark Summary

Medians on Windows x64, Python 3.13 (details, versions, and methodology in [docs/architecture/benchmarks.md](docs/architecture/benchmarks.md) and `benchmarks/`):

| Scenario | `oxide_parse` | Nearest competitors | Run |
|---|---|---|---|
| Catalog 10,000 items + noise (6.2 MiB) | `stream` **71.9 ms**, `lite` **103.1 ms** | `frostwork` 127.5 ms, `selectolax` 445.1 ms, `bs4+lxml` 8659.6 ms | v7.2 full |
| Early Exit (`og:title` from `<head>`, 875 KiB) | `auto` (`stream`) **1.43 ms** | `scraper` (v8.4.1 pre-stream meta) 81.89 ms | v8.5 paired |
| Hybrid HTML + `__NEXT_DATA__` (1,000 records) | `lite` **4.34 ms**, `stream` **6.05 ms** | `selectolax + json.loads` 2.45 ms, `lxml + json.loads` 5.17 ms | v8.0 full |
| Batch 32 docs x 500 items (9.8 MiB) | `stream` (Rayon) **51.6 ms** | `stream` (loop) 121.7 ms, `selectolax` (loop) 487.7 ms | v8.0 full |
| HTML to Markdown (300 blocks) | `lite` **1.51 ms**, `scraper` **7.26 ms** | `html2text` 140.5 ms, `markdownify` 197.4 ms | v8.5 paired |

# DSL Cheatsheet (`T`)

Everything you can write in a schema on one page. Full signatures live in [reference/python_api.md](../reference/python_api.md).

```python
from oxide_parse import T, compile, follow, paginate, if_, coalesce
```

## Reading Pipelines

`T` represents the current node or value. `T.css(".card").css("h2").text()` reads left to right: find cards, find headings inside them, read the text. Before `compile()`, a `T` chain only records operations without touching any document.

Four core rules:

- `.text()`, `.attr()`, and `.html()` on a node list read the **first** node. To collect every match, use `.map(...)`.
- When a step finds nothing, `None` flows down the rest of the pipeline without raising. `.default(x)` supplies a fallback; `.required()` turns `None` into an error.
- Arguments to `default`, `if_`, `coalesce`, `eq`, etc. are evaluated against the **current context** (the card inside `map`), not against the left-hand value.
- Never use Python `and`/`or`/`not`/`if` inside schemas (`bool(expr)` raises `TypeError`). Use `&`, `|`, `~`, and `if_()`.

## Navigation

| Task | Expression |
|---|---|
| All CSS matches | `T.css("a.item")` |
| XPath 1.0 | `T.xpath("//h1")` (DOM engines only) |
| First / last match | `.first()`, `.last()` |
| By index | `T.css("li")[0]`, `.at(1)` (or `.last()` for the final item) |
| Slices | `T[1:]`, `T[:5]`, `.slice(1, 4)`, `.rest()` (everything after first) |
| Tree traversal | `.parent()`, `.children()`, `.root()` |
| JSON key | `T["props"]["items"]`, `.key("props")` |
| Direct children of card | `T.css(":scope > .title")` |

```python
html = "<ul><li>1</li><li>2</li><li>3</li><li>4</li></ul>"
schema = {
    "middle": T.css("li").slice(1, 3).map(T.text()),
    "last": T.css("li")[-1:].map(T.text()),
}
print(compile(schema, backend="auto").extract(html))
```

```text
{'middle': ['2', '3'], 'last': ['4']}
```

## Extraction

| Task | Expression |
|---|---|
| Text | `.text()` (`<script>`/`<style>` descendants skipped automatically) |
| Joined & trimmed text | `.text(" ", strip=True)` |
| Excluding subtrees | `.text(" ", strip=True, without=".ad, .share")` |
| `<br>` as newline | `.text(" ", strip=True, br="\n")` |
| Attribute | `.attr("href")` |
| Attribute presence | `.has_attr("disabled")` (handles valueless flags like `<button disabled>`) |
| HTML | `.html()`, `.inner_html()` |
| Markdown | `.markdown(without=".ad")` (DOM engines) |
| Prompt-sized skeleton | `.distill(max_chars=8000)` |
| Item index in `map` | `T.index()` |
| Count / presence | `.count()`, `.exists()` |
| Metadata value | `T.meta("title")` |

```python
html = '<div class="d">Screen: OLED<br>Refresh: 120 Hz<span class="ad">promo</span></div>'
schema = {"spec": T.css(".d").text(" ", strip=True, br="\n", without=".ad")}
print(compile(schema, backend="auto").extract(html))
```

```text
{'spec': 'Screen: OLED\nRefresh: 120 Hz'}
```

## Strings & Types

| Task | Expression |
|---|---|
| Trim & case | `.strip()`, `.lower()`, `.upper()` |
| Replace | `.replace("old", "new")` |
| Split / join | `.split(",")`, `.join(", ")` |
| Regex | `.regex(r"(\d+)", 1)`, `.regex_all(r"\d+")` |
| Numbers | `.int()`, `.float()` |
| Booleans | `.bool()` |
| Resolve relative URL | `.url()` or `.url("https://base/")` |

`.int()` and `.float()` handle currency symbols and localized separators out of the box: `"$1,299.50"` -> `1299.5`, `"19,99 €"` -> `19.99`, `"12 990 ₽"` -> `12990`, `"1.299,50"` -> `1299.5`. A single comma followed by three digits (`1,299`) is treated as a thousands separator unless the integer part is `0` or longer than three digits, and `"Model-3"` does not read `-3`. If no number appears in the text, conversion raises an extraction error rather than returning `None`.

## Nulls & Fallbacks

| Task | Expression |
|---|---|
| Default value | `.default("—")` |
| Required value | `.required()` |
| Treat blanks/empty as missing | `.non_empty().default("—")` |
| First non-missing alternative | `coalesce(T.attr("title"), T.text())` |

```python
html = "<p></p>"
schema = {
    "price": T.css(".price").text().float(),
    "label": T.css(".label").text().default("—"),
}
print(compile(schema).extract(html))
```

```text
{'price': None, 'label': '—'}
```

## Collections & Logic

| Task | Expression |
|---|---|
| Map items | `.map({...})`, `.map(T.text())` |
| Quarantine bad records | `.map({...}, on_error="skip")` or `"null"` |
| Flatten nested lists | `.flat_map(...)` |
| Filter | `.filter(T.attr("data-on") == "1")` |
| Comparisons | `==`, `!=`, `.contains()`, `.startswith()`, `.endswith()` |
| Boolean logic | `&`, `\|`, `~` |
| Conditional | `if_(cond, then, otherwise)` |

```python
html = '''<ul>
  <li data-on="1" data-hot>A</li>
  <li data-on="0">B</li>
  <li data-on="1" title="Featured">C</li>
</ul>'''
schema = {
    "items": T.css("li").filter(T.attr("data-on") == "1").map({
        "name": T.text(),
        "hot": if_(T.has_attr("data-hot"), "yes", "no"),
        "label": coalesce(T.attr("title"), T.text()),
    }),
}
print(compile(schema).extract(html))
```

```text
{'items': [{'name': 'A', 'hot': 'yes', 'label': 'A'}, {'name': 'C', 'hot': 'no', 'label': 'Featured'}]}
```

## Flat Markup

Pages often dump sections sequentially inside one container: a heading, a few paragraphs, another heading. Without wrapper elements per section, use `group_by`:

```python
html = '''<div class="specs">
  <h3>Display</h3><p>14"</p><p>OLED</p>
  <h3>Memory</h3><p>32 GB</p>
</div>'''
schema = {
    "specs": T.css(".specs").group_by("h3").map({
        "section": T.first().text(),
        "items": T.rest().map(T.text()),
    }),
}
print(compile(schema, backend="auto").extract(html))
```

```text
{'specs': [{'section': 'Display', 'items': ['14"', 'OLED']}, {'section': 'Memory', 'items': ['32 GB']}]}
```

Inside `group_by(...).map(...)`, the current node list is the group itself: `T.first()` is the header and `T.rest()` holds everything after it. If you only need `{"header": ..., "items": [...]}` pairs, `T.css(".specs").sections("h3", items="p")` is even shorter.

For label/value tables, `T.kv("Weight")` finds a `th`/`dt`/`td`/`label`/`strong`/`b`/`span`/`div` matching that label and returns its following sibling element:

```python
html = "<table><tr><th>Weight</th><td>1.1 kg</td></tr></table>"
print(compile({"weight": T.kv("Weight").text().float()}).extract(html))
```

```text
{'weight': 1.1}
```

## Hybrid Data & Sub-queries

More details live in dedicated guides:

| Pattern | Expression | Guide |
|---|---|---|
| JSON inside `<script>` | `T.css("script#__NEXT_DATA__").text().parse_json()["props"]` | [04](04_hybrid_html_json.md) |
| JS variable JSON | `.js_json("window.__STATE__")["cart"]` | [04](04_hybrid_html_json.md) |
| JSON-LD | `T.json_ld("Product")[0]["name"]` | [04](04_hybrid_html_json.md) |
| OpenGraph / Twitter | `T.meta_tags()`, `T.meta_tags(values="first")["og:image"]` | [04](04_hybrid_html_json.md) |
| Self-healing selector | `T.css(".price", adaptive="price")` | [05](05_adaptive_and_repair.md) |
| Linked page sub-query | `follow(request=..., schema=..., meta=...)` | [06](06_follow_and_crawling.md) |
| `next`-page pagination | `paginate(items=..., next=..., max_pages=..., max_items=...)` | [06](06_follow_and_crawling.md) |

<!-- FILE: docs/reference/ir_spec.md -->

# IR Specification (`Expr` and `Op`)

The IR is the JSON/YAML intermediate representation of a schema. `to_ir(schema)` compiles the Python DSL (`T`) into IR, `decompile(ir)` reconstructs Python code from IR, and Rust `Plan::compile` executes IR directly.

Machine-readable JSON Schema (Draft 2020-12): [ir.schema.json](../../python/oxide_parse/ir.schema.json) (also returned by `oxide_parse.ir_schema()`). The single source of truth is [ir_spec.py](../../python/oxide_parse/ir_spec.py), verified against the JSON Schema and Rust AST by `python scripts/gen_ir_schema.py --check`.

## `Expr` Nodes

Every `Expr` node is a JSON object with exactly one of these four keys:

| Kind | Shape | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `pipe` | `{"pipe": [op, ...]}` | Sequence of operations evaluated over the current context |
| `object` | `{"object": {"field": expr, ...}}` | Dictionary of named field expressions |
| `list` | `{"list": [expr, ...]}` | List of sub-expressions |
| `lit` | `{"lit": <json_value>}` | Any JSON-compatible literal value |

## `Op` Operations

### Unit Operations (`UNIT_OPS`)

Serialized inside `"pipe"` as plain strings:

- Navigation: `"parent"`, `"children"`, `"root"`, `"first"`, `"last"`.
- Extraction: `"text"`, `"html"`, `"inner_html"`, `"index"`.
- Collections & nulls: `"count"`, `"exists"`, `"required"`, `"non_empty"`.
- Strings: `"strip"`, `"lower"`, `"upper"`.
- Conversions & logic: `"int"`, `"float"`, `"bool"`, `"parse_json"`, `"not"`.

### Single-Argument Scalar Operations

Serialized as `{"<name>": arg}`:

| Op | Argument Type | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `css` | `str` | CSS selector |
| `xpath` | `str` | XPath 1.0 expression |
| `key` | `str` | Object key lookup |
| `attr` | `str` | Attribute lookup |
| `has_attr` | `str` | Attribute presence check |
| `meta` | `str` | Metadata dictionary key lookup |
| `split` | `str` | Split string by delimiter |
| `join` | `str` | Join list by delimiter |
| `at` | `uint` (`int >= 0`) | Zero-based element index (Python `at` also handles negative indices; JSON Schema validates `uint`; use `slice` for general slices) |

*Note:* `python/oxide_parse/ir_spec.py` defines `at` as `uint`.

### Expression Operations

Serialized as `{"<name>": <Expr>}` (or `{"coalesce": [<Expr>, ...]}`):

- `map`, `flat_map`, `filter`
- `default`
- `eq`, `ne`, `contains`, `starts_with`, `ends_with`
- `and`, `or`
- `coalesce` (`list[Expr]`)

### Structured Operations (`STRUCT_OPS`)

Serialized as `{"<name>": {field: value, ...}}`:

| Op | Fields (`*` = required) |
|---|---|
| `slice` | `start?: int \| null`, `stop?: int \| null` |
| `text_opts` | `sep?: str`, `strip?: bool`, `without?: str \| null`, `br?: str \| null` |
| `markdown` | `without?: str \| null` |
| `distill` | `keep?: uint \| null`, `max_text?: uint \| null`, `max_chars?: uint \| null` |
| `adaptive` | `css*: str`, `key*: str`, `threshold?: float \| null` |
| `map_opts` | `body*: Expr`, `on_error?: "raise" \| "null" \| "skip"` |
| `resolve_url` | `base?: Expr \| null` |
| `js_json` | `var?: str \| null` |
| `sections` | `header*: str`, `items?: str \| null` |
| `group_by` | `header*: str`, `items?: str \| null` |
| `json_ld` | `schema_type?: str \| null` |
| `meta_tags` | `prefixes?: list[str]`, `values?: "auto" \| "first" \| "list" \| null` |
| `replace` | `from*: str`, `to*: str` |
| `regex` | `pattern*: str`, `group?: uint` |
| `regex_all` | `pattern*: str`, `group?: uint` |
| `if` | `cond*: Expr`, `then*: Expr`, `otherwise*: Expr` |
| `follow` | `request*: Expr`, `meta?: Expr \| null`, `schema*: Expr` |
| `paginate` | `items*: Expr`, `next*: Expr`, `meta?: Expr \| null`, `max_pages?: posint \| null`, `max_items?: posint \| null` |

## IR Validation

`oxide_parse.validate_ir(ir, backend="auto") -> list[str]` walks the entire IR tree and collects every issue at once with paths (`$.field[0].op: message`) instead of stopping at the first error. When the native module is loaded, it also checks compilation against `backend` (CSS/XPath syntax and engine compatibility).

CLI equivalents:

```bash
oxide-parse validate schema.json --backend auto
oxide-parse ir-schema
```

<!-- FILE: docs/ai/prompt_generate_schema.md -->

# Prompt: Generate an `oxide_parse` Schema from HTML

Instead of having an LLM emit fragile scraper code with manual loops, `try/except`, and `None` checks, ask it for a declarative `T` schema. `oxide_parse` validates the schema at compile time and executes it in Rust.

## Workflow

1. Shrink raw HTML down to a compact skeleton so scripts and repeated cards do not flood the prompt window:

```bash
oxide-parse distill page.html --max-chars 8000 -o skeleton.html
```

2. Copy the system prompt below (or print the compact CLI prompt via `oxide-parse prompt generate`).
3. Send `skeleton.html` plus your target field specification to your model.
4. Validate and test locally — `validate` reports every error with its JSON path, and `run` prints the selected engine and extracted JSON:

```bash
oxide-parse validate schema.py
oxide-parse run schema.py page.html --backend auto --explain
```

## System Prompt (Copy & Paste)

```markdown
You write declarative extraction schemas for `oxide_parse` (Python DSL -> IR -> Rust engine).
Given sample HTML (possibly shrunk via `distill(html)`) and a target field specification, produce a valid, minimal, high-throughput `oxide_parse` schema.

## DSL Rules
1. Import: `from oxide_parse import T, compile, follow, paginate, if_, coalesce`
2. Root schema: a Python `dict` whose values are `T` chains, nested `dict`/`list`, or literals.
3. Never use Python `if/else`, `and/or/not`, `for`, or `try/except` inside `schema`:
   - Use `&`, `|`, `~` (or `.and_()`, `.or_()`, `.not_()`) instead of `and / or / not`.
   - Use `if_(cond, then, otherwise)` instead of ternary expressions.
   - Use `coalesce(a, b)` or `.non_empty().default(...)` instead of `a or b`.
4. Navigation & extraction:
   - `T.css(sel)` (pass `adaptive="unique_key", threshold=0.5` only for fragile selectors). Check every tag and class against the provided HTML; never invent selectors.
   - `T.xpath(expr)` (DOM engines only).
   - `T.text(sep=None, strip=False, without=None, br=None)` (`<script>` and `<style>` content is skipped automatically).
   - `T.attr("href")`, `T.has_attr("disabled")`, `T.html()`, `T.inner_html()`, `T.markdown(without=...)`, `T.distill(max_chars=...)`.
   - `T.first()`, `T.last()`, `T[0]`, `T[1:]`, `T.slice(a, b)`, `T.rest()`, `T["key"]`, `T.parent()`, `T.children()`, `T.root()`, `T.index()`, `T.meta("key")`.
   - `T.count()`, `T.exists()`, `T.map(body, on_error="raise"|"skip"|"null")`, `T.flat_map(body)`, `T.filter(pred)`.
   - On a node list, `.text()`, `.attr()`, `.html()` read only the **first** node. Use `.map(...)` to extract lists.
5. Strings, numbers, URLs (null-safe: missing elements flow as `None` without raising):
   - `.strip()`, `.lower()`, `.upper()`, `.replace(old, new)`, `.split(sep)`, `.join(sep)`
   - `.regex(pattern, group=0)`, `.regex_all(pattern, group=0)`
   - `.int()`, `.float()` (parse `"$1,299.50"`, `"19,99 €"`, `"12 990 ₽"` directly without `.replace()`), `.bool()`
   - `.default(val)`, `.required()`, `.non_empty()`
   - `.url(base=None)` — RFC 3986 resolution against `base`, `meta["base_url"]`, or `<base href>`
6. Hybrid HTML + JSON & flat markup:
   - `.parse_json()["a"]["b"]` — JSON in `<script id="__NEXT_DATA__">` (cached per run, zero-copy path navigation)
   - `.js_json("window.__STATE__")["a"]` — JSON inside JS assignments / `JSON.parse(...)`
   - `T.json_ld("Product")[0]["offers"]["price"]` — JSON-LD with `@graph` unfolding
   - `T.meta_tags(("og:", "twitter:"), values="first")` — `<meta>` tags (`values="first"` when chaining `.url()`/`.strip()`)
   - `T.sections("h3", items="p")` or `T.group_by("h3").map({"title": T.first().text(), "items": T.rest().map(T.text().strip())})` — flat sibling sections
   - `T.kv("Weight").text().strip()` — sibling value next to a label cell
7. Zero-IO crawling & pagination:
   - `follow(request={"url": T.css("a").attr("href").url()}, schema={...}, meta={...})` (no `url=` kwarg).
   - `paginate(items=T.css(".item").map({...}), next=T.css("a.next").attr("href").url(), max_pages=5, max_items=None)`.

## Performance (Prefer `stream`)
- Stay inside the `stream`-compatible subset with `backend="auto"` when possible:
  - Root `dict` with `T.css(...).text()/attr()/count()/exists()`, `T.meta_tags()`, and `T.css(".card").map({...}, on_error="skip")`.
  - `:scope > .child`, `text(sep=..., strip=..., br=..., without=...)`, `.url()`, `.parse_json()`, `.js_json()`, `T.slice()`/`T.rest()` all stream.
  - Avoid `+`, `~`, `:has()`, `:contains()`, `:last-child`, `parent()`, `xpath()`, and `filter()` when standard CSS or streaming filters suffice.
- Add `on_error="skip"` on `.map(...)` lists whenever records call `.int()`, `.float()`, or `.required()`.
- Only add `adaptive=` on selectors prone to breakage (`adaptive` forces `auto` onto a DOM engine).

## Output Format
1. One Python code block defining `schema = {...}` and `plan = compile(schema, backend="auto")`.
2. Two or three concise notes stating which engine `auto` selects (`stream` or `lite`/`scraper`) and any required `meta` keys (e.g., `base_url`).
```


---
<!-- FILE: docs/ai/prompt_migrate.md -->

# Prompt: Migrate Scrapers to `oxide_parse`

## When You Do Not Need an LLM

Declarative Crawl4AI JSON strategies (`JsonCssExtractionStrategy`, `JsonXPathExtractionStrategy`, `CrawlerRunConfig` dumps) and flat Scrapy/Parsel selector maps (`{"title": "h1::text", "tags": ["li::text"]}`) convert deterministically in milliseconds:

```bash
oxide-parse migrate --from crawl4ai strategy.json --format python -o schema.py
oxide-parse migrate --from selector-map selectors.json --format python -o schema.py
```

Or from Python: `oxide_parse.migrate.from_crawl4ai_code(strategy)` and `from_selector_map_code(mapping)`.

For imperative code written with BeautifulSoup, Scrapy, lxml, Selectolax, or Scrapling, use the mapping table and prompt below (or print the source-specific CLI prompt via `oxide-parse prompt migrate --from bs4`).

```bash
oxide-parse prompt migrate --from bs4   # choices: bs4, scrapy, selectolax, lxml, crawl4ai
```

## Primitive Mapping Table

| Source | Legacy Code | `oxide_parse` Equivalent |
|---|---|---|
| **Crawl4AI** | `JsonCssExtractionStrategy({"baseSelector": ".card", "fields": [...]})` | `T.css(".card").map({...})` |
| **Crawl4AI** | `{"name": "p", "selector": ".price", "type": "text"}` | `"p": T.css(".price").text(strip=True)` |
| **Crawl4AI** | `{"name": "u", "selector": "a", "type": "attribute", "attribute": "href"}` | `"u": T.css("a").attr("href")` |
| **Crawl4AI** | `result.markdown` | `T.css("article").markdown()` / `oxide_parse.markdown(html)` |
| **Scrapy / Parsel** | `sel.css("h1::text").get(default="")` | `T.css("h1").text().default("")` |
| **Scrapy / Parsel** | `sel.css("a::attr(href)").getall()` | `T.css("a").map(T.attr("href"))` |
| **Scrapy / Parsel** | `sel.css(".p::text").re_first(r"(\d+)")` | `T.css(".p").text().regex(r"(\d+)", 1)` |
| **Scrapy / Parsel** | `response.urljoin(href)` | `T.attr("href").url()` (+ `meta={"base_url": url}`) |
| **Scrapy / Parsel** | `response.follow(href, callback=self.parse_item, cb_kwargs=...)` | `follow(request=T.attr("href").url(), schema=..., meta=...)` |
| **Next-page loop** | `while next_url: ... next_url = sel.css("a.next::attr(href)").get()` | `paginate(items=..., next=T.css("a.next").attr("href").url())` |
| **BeautifulSoup** | `soup.select_one("h1").get_text(" ", strip=True)` | `T.css("h1").text(" ", strip=True)` |
| **BeautifulSoup** | `for x in el.select(".ad"): x.decompose(); el.get_text()` | `T.text(without=".ad")` |
| **BeautifulSoup** | `float(re.sub(r"[^\d.]", "", txt))` | `T.text().float()` |
| **Selectolax** | `tree.css_first(".name").text(strip=True)` | `T.css(".name").text().strip()` |
| **Selectolax** | `tree.strip_tags(["script", "style", ".ad"])` | `T.text(without=".ad")` (`script`/`style` are already omitted) |
| **Scrapling** | `page.css(".price", adaptive=True).first.text` | `T.css(".price", adaptive="price").text()` |
| **Scrapling** | `page.css(".card", adaptive=True)` (list of cards) | `T.css(".card", adaptive="cards").map({...})` |
| **Next.js / Nuxt** | `json.loads(soup.select_one("#__NEXT_DATA__").text)["props"]...` | `T.css("script#__NEXT_DATA__").text().parse_json()["props"]...` |

## System Prompt (Copy & Paste)

```markdown
You migrate scrapers to `oxide_parse` (Python DSL + Rust execution engine).
Convert the provided extraction code or JSON strategy (Crawl4AI, Scrapy/Parsel, BeautifulSoup, lxml, Selectolax, Scrapling) into a clean declarative `oxide_parse` schema.

## Migration Rules
1. Replace imperative `for item in ...` loops with `.map({...})`.
2. Remove `if el is not None else None` boilerplate — every chain is null-safe by default; use `.default(...)` for explicit fallbacks.
3. Replace manual price cleanup (`re.sub`, `.replace("$", "").replace(",", "")`) with `.float()` or `.int()` (built-in support for `"$1,299.50"`, `"19,99 €"`, `"12 990 ₽"`).
4. Replace `decompose()` / `strip_tags()` calls with `T.text(sep=" ", strip=True, without="...")` (`<script>` and `<style>` are skipped automatically).
5. Convert inline `json.loads(...)` calls on script tags to `.parse_json()[...]`, `.js_json("var_name")[...]`, or `T.json_ld("Type")`.
6. Convert link-following logic (`requests.get`, `response.follow`) to Zero-IO `follow(request={"url": ...}, schema={...}, meta={...})` and next-page loops to `paginate(items=..., next=...)`, with a minimal `plan.extract(html, fetch=...)` example.
7. Convert Scrapling `adaptive=True` lookups to `T.css(sel, adaptive="<field_key>")` and pass `adaptive_store="store.json"` to `compile()`.
8. Scrapy `::text` and `::attr(x)` pseudo-elements are invalid CSS in `oxide_parse` — use `.text()` and `.attr("x")` pipeline methods instead. Note that Parsel `::text` returns direct child text nodes whereas `T.text()` returns descendant text.
9. When direct children inside a card are needed (CSS `> .title`), write `:scope > .title`.

## Output
1. Complete runnable `oxide_parse` snippet (`schema = ...`, `plan = compile(schema, backend="auto")`).
2. **Migration Notes** (3-5 concise bullets: removed boilerplate, chosen engine, subtle semantic differences).
3. Keep non-extraction code (DB persistence, auth, custom session scheduling) outside `schema` around `plan.extract()` / `plan.start()`.
```


---
<!-- FILE: docs/ai/prompt_self_healing.md -->

# Prompt: Self-Healing Broken Selectors (`repair` / `repair_batch`)

When an `adaptive` selector stops matching and fingerprint relocation falls below `threshold`, `oxide_parse` emits a repair request to your callback — typically backed by an LLM.

See also [05_adaptive_and_repair.md](../guide/05_adaptive_and_repair.md).

## Input Payload (`repair_batch`)

`plan.extract(html, repair_batch=ask_llm)` and `plan.extract_or_repair(html, repair_batch=ask_llm)` group all fields that broke within the same HTML container into one payload:

- `doc`, `url`: document identifier and URL (if any);
- `scope`: `"container"` (distilled old parent container) or `"page"` (whole distilled page if the container was missing);
- `skeleton`: shrunk HTML skeleton of that region;
- `schema`: compiled schema IR;
- `fields`: list of `{id, key, css, fingerprint, previous_error?}` objects:
  - `fingerprint` holds old `tag`, `attrs`, `text`, `path`, `parent`, `prev`, `next`, `children`, and up to 3 previous extracted `samples`;
  - `previous_error` appears on a retry when the model's earlier selector failed CSS parsing.

Once the callback returns valid CSS selectors, extraction re-runs cleanly, and `extract_or_repair` returns an updated `Plan` ready to export via `res.plan.to_python()`.

## System Prompt for Your Model

```markdown
You repair broken CSS selectors for `oxide_parse`.
Input is a JSON object with:
- `skeleton`: distilled HTML of the target area (`scope`: `"container"` or `"page"`).
- `fields`: list of broken fields, each with `key`, old `css`, `fingerprint` (old tag, attrs, path, and `samples` of previous values), and optional `previous_error` if your last CSS had invalid syntax.

Rules:
1. Return ONLY a valid JSON object mapping `{key: new_css_selector}`. Omit a key if the data is genuinely absent from `skeleton`.
2. Use standard CSS Selectors only (tags, `#id`, `.class`, `[attr=val]`, `>`, ` `, `:nth-child()`, `:not()`, `:scope`).
3. NEVER use non-standard syntax like `::text`, `::attr(...)`, `:contains-text(...)`, or XPath.
4. Prefer stable semantic attributes (`data-testid`, `itemprop`, `aria-label`, semantic classes) over brittle hashed classes or deep `nth-child` chains.
5. If `previous_error` is present, fix the exact syntax issue reported there.
```

## Wiring in Python

```python
import json

SYSTEM_PROMPT = "..."  # system prompt above

def ask_llm(batch: dict) -> dict[str, str]:
    payload = {
        "scope": batch["scope"],
        "skeleton": batch["skeleton"],
        "fields": [
            {k: f[k] for k in ("key", "css", "fingerprint", "previous_error") if k in f}
            for f in batch["fields"]
        ],
    }
    raw = your_llm_call(system=SYSTEM_PROMPT, user=json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False))
    return json.loads(raw)

res = plan.extract_or_repair(html, repair_batch=ask_llm)
if res.repaired:
    with open("schema.py", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(res.plan.to_python())
```
